Marissa / team — quick technical summary from the on-call serving side after a 08:25 triage:
- Observed symptoms: Dedicated pool "dedicated-us-west-2-cc-dc4781" shows GPU utilization pegged at 97–99% across nodes, active queue depth rising from 12 -> 64 over 20m. KV-cache hit rate is lower than expected for this workload (~18% vs typical 45%).
- Root signal: we are seeing a significant amount of short, chatty requests from a small number of hosted tenants routing through the same allocation class. There is a routing policy regression in the rollout (INF-8921) that allowed some hosted traffic to bypass isolation checks and consume headroom.

Immediate mitigations we can enact (ordered by speed/impact):
1) Emergency traffic shed: divert non-reserved traffic off the dedicated pool and enforce isolation policy (ETA 10–15m).
2) Temporary model fallback: switch ClearCommerce routes to a compatible quantized variant (8-bit) with equivalent semantics — reduces GPU time per token ~25% (ETA 20–30m with a rolling routing change).
3) Enable emergency burst capacity (provisioned on shared pool) for 60–120m — requires exec approval for cross-tenant burst billing (ETA to provision ~30m after approval).

I'll attach a snapshot of current capacity (capacity_snapshot_20270930.png) and a candidate patch that enforces the routing check (candidate_patch_0929.diff). We should combine 1) and 2) immediately; 3) if the queue doesn't improve.
